clue.text: A heavy supper can lead to it

definitions.text: A heavy supper can lead to it

parts.words: A heavy supper can lead to it
parts.note: reads like a big late meal causing indigestion, but a heavy supper is someone who sups (drinks) heavily, and what follows is a hangover

explanation.surface: A warning that a big evening meal can bring on some unpleasant consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supper' looks like an evening meal; here it is one who sups, i.e. drinks, so a heavy supper is a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the hangover a heavy drinker suffers on waking the next day.

parts.note: PS is the standard abbreviation for a private secretary
to revise a text is to alter it, so revises means alters

explanation.surface: A minister's aide edits some volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalm books, volumes containing the psalms for worship, are a kind of book.

clue.text: Spanish wine made from 18 books, partly

parts.note: Jer is the usual abbreviation for the biblical book of Jeremiah
Ez is an abbreviation for the biblical book of Ezekiel (some reserve it for Ezra)

explanation.surface: A sherry somehow derived from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is BIBLICAL (18 down), so '18 books' are two books of the Bible, given 'partly', i.e. in shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerez is the Andalusian town whose name gave English the word sherry, and the name is used for the wine itself.

parts.note: to plant something is to set it growing, so grow stands for plant
pot is a slang name for cannabis

explanation.surface: An exclamation pointing out where to raise a cannabis crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of a container for growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is the container in which one grows a plant, cannabis included.

indicators.note: sounding signals that we want a word pronounced like the phrase that follows

parts.note: crocs, short for crocodiles, are dangerous animals in water

explanation.surface: Something unsettling sounds menacing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are earthenware pots or jars.

clue.text: Plants found in rolling acres, nine

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters tumbling over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Factories located amid nine undulating acres of countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works, and canneries are works where food is tinned.

clue.text: Pitch tents where enclosure has electricity supply

parts.note: enc is the abbreviation for enclosure, as written at the foot of a letter
amp, short for ampere, is loosely taken as a measure of electricity supply

explanation.surface: Campers put up their tents in a field that has a power hook-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up camp is to put up tents for the night.

definitions.meaning: one drink too many is what brings on a hangover the next day
the number nine is one more than eight, literally one beyond that figure

explanation.surface: A hangover might result from the number nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is the hangover clue; '9' is not a cross-reference but the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having drunk too much, which causes a hangover; nine also is literally a single unit beyond eight.

clue.text: He'll store brews for the landlord

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stir, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man says he will keep beers in stock for the pub owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosteller is an archaic word for an innkeeper, someone who keeps a hostelry.

clue.text: Grandma goes back to Scottish town

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: nanna is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother returns to a town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Annan is a town in Dumfries and Galloway in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Two familiar chaps bring water from the hills

parts.note: Mal is a familiar short form of the name Malcolm
Vern is a familiar short form of the name Vernon

explanation.surface: A couple of mates fetch spring water down from the uplands.
explanation.definitionFit: Malvern water is a bottled spring water drawn from the Malvern Hills in Worcestershire, England.

definitions.note: read as It is, with It the crossword shorthand for Italian vermouth

indicators.note: moulding is reshaping, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Something is resting on a shaped piece of zinc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It', as in gin and It, is Italian vermouth; 'moulding' rearranges ONAZINC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinzano is a brand of Italian vermouth, which is what It means in gin and It.

parts.note: Romeo is the radio alphabet word for the letter R
to say yes is to agree

explanation.surface: A lover consents to supply the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain, so ryes are glasses of it.

parts.note: looks like a statement about a sign of possession, but read as the mark in the word It's it names the punctuation printed there, which also shows ownership

explanation.surface: Something is described as the sign that shows who owns a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark in 'It's' itself shows a missing letter, not ownership, which is the clue's wink.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma punctuation mark shows possession, as in the cat's bowl.

clue.text: Support for clergy in theatrical setting

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A call for clergy to be backed within the world of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted cloth hung at the back of a stage as scenery.

definitions.meaning: ... coffee is the powdered kind made by adding hot water

explanation.surface: A brief pause for a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment, and also the quick soluble kind of coffee.

indicators.note: a product is something made, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: An Australian woman's beer is the finest thing she makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheila' is Australian slang for a woman, so 'Sheila's beer' is the Australian slang word for beer; 'product' rearranges HERBEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records the word as Australian slang for beer.

parts.note: craft looks like a skill such as cookery, but here means vessels; the same word also names pans that cook food by vapour

explanation.surface: A culinary skill employed in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' can be plural: boats powered by vapour, and also pots for cooking vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats driven by vapour power share their name with kitchen pans that cook by vapour.

clue.text: Drink crushed lilac, as prescribed in the good book

definitions.text: as prescribed in the good book

parts.note: to bib is an old verb meaning to drink, as in wine-bibber

indicators.note: crushed suggests the flowers broken up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remedy of crushed lilac flowers in a drink, as directed by scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: What scripture prescribes is according to the Bible, hence scriptural.

clue.text: Lame goalie, who caused the beating on the 12th

definitions.text: who caused the beating on the 12th

parts.note: a game leg is a lame one
a goalie is a goalkeeper, or keeper

explanation.surface: An injured goalkeeper who was responsible for a thrashing on the twelfth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12th is the Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, when grouse shooting begins in Britain; beaters drive the birds, organised by the estate's warden.
explanation.definitionFit: The estate warden organises the beaters who drive grouse towards the guns on shooting days.

definitions.meaning: Madge is a nickname for the singer Madonna, so this reads as Madge plus s
madge is an old dialect name for a magpie

explanation.surface: Birds belonging to a famous singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's nickname takes a possessive s, and the dialect name for magpie takes a plural s.

clue.text: Puccini's second opera version of "Bully Zeus and Me"

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so the letters are rearranged
second picks the second letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A new production of a Puccini work given a lurid tabloid title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes U from PUCCINI; 'version of' rearranges U with OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Zeus took the form of a bull to carry off the princess, so the title sums up her story.

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A bright academic lives in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the English city; it is Abe Lincoln, with L 'residing in' him.
explanation.definitionFit: Able and clever both describe someone capable and talented.

clue.text: Doctors keep example on 1 of what's left after 3, 5, 8, 12, 13, 17 and 25 are downed

definitions.text: what's left after 3, 5, 8, 12, 13, 17 and 25 are downed

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
eg, for example, stands for example

explanation.surface: Physicians cite the remains of a night of drinking the morning after.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-referenced answers are drinks or drink vessels; 'on 1' (THE MORNING AFTER) links the sediment to the hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left at the bottom of a glass or bottle once the drink is finished.

definitions.meaning: looks like a con man leading people on, but means a player of a stringed instrument entertaining them

explanation.surface: A con man who deceived people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a cheat, and also a violinist who plays a stringed instrument.

definitions.meaning: read as It is, with It the crossword shorthand for Italian vermouth
piece is slang for a gun, and the ... rifle is an old firearm

explanation.surface: Something is described as an antique French item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Martini-Henry rifle was British, with an action designed by a Swiss-Hungarian engineer, so 'French' looks like the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a brand of Italian vermouth and also an old breech-loading rifle.

indicators.note: held in means contained inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something happened back in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occasion, something that takes place.

clue.text: News item: soldier's picture showing axes

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a graph is a diagram plotted against axes

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a soldier's photo showing hatchets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like hatchets; it is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the word as a short newspaper report, a news item.
